1947, August 4
The following is a faithful transcription of a photo copy of a typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O. F. M. Cap.
PAX ET BONUM
Capuchin Franciscan Fathers
ST. FELIX FRIARY Huntington, Indiana
August 4, 1947
Mrs. John McCloskey Seattle, Washington
My Dear Sister Mary Gevevieve:
God bless you and all yours. I hope this finds you well as, than is be to God it leaves me.
I really do not know when I've written you last or how long I've been wanting to write you, though I hardly think there is a day passes that I do not remember you. However, your son John now our promising, young Jesuite Father Mc Closkey gave us the pleasure of a visit here yesterday; and so, I determined on writing you at least a few lines before letting it linger longer.
Only a week or two ago I learned from some good friends of ours - O'Donnells - of Father John's presence so near, even in Chicago. The had been figuering on driving down ever since early in June, when they were very kind to myself and our Nep- hew Bernard Maurice, when we went out to St. Paul and from there visited Fr. Maurice Joachim in Gracefille.
Our visit to poor, dear Maurice had to be short under the circumstances but I think we all quite enjoyed it. Both Fa- thers Maurice and Edward are quite well. Thanks be to God. We had planned on a solemn Mass on the 36th anniversary of M's ord- ination but the chapel is very small - just temporary; so I ser- ved his Mass and he surprised me how well he was able and served mine. It was Wednesday, the anniversary of his First Holy Mass instead of Monday of ordination and I had promissed the Father Guardian who at the time was not well, that I'd try hard to be back for Sunday. I had quite an important sick-call to make in
